provenance.prompt:
Create one original production sprite sheet for Piper Quickstep performing a basketball rebound catch. Use the supplied accepted Piper sheets only to preserve her identity, clothing and rendering style. Piper is an athletic adult human woman with warm-brown skin, a bright orange high ponytail tied behind her head, a russet-red basketball uniform with cream speed stripes and trim, and matching red/cream trainers. Preserve her face, hair, skin, athletic proportions, full anatomy and uniform. Keep her kit blank of text, logos and numbers.

Canvas and layout: transparent RGBA, exactly 1536x1024 pixels, three equal columns by two equal rows, each cell 512x512. Place exactly five complete, clearly distinct poses in row-major cells 0 through 4. Cell 5 (bottom-right) must remain fully transparent and empty. Center each whole figure in its cell at a consistent scale and same image-right three-quarter view. Maintain at least 64 fully transparent pixels between every body part, including ponytail, fingertips and shoes, and all four cell edges. No part may touch or cross a cell edge. Do not overlap poses.

Five-pose sequence, exact order:
0. Ready / track: balanced low rebound stance, knees flexed, chin and eyes tracking an unseen ball above; elbows bent and both empty hands open near the upper chest, ready to jump.
1. Load and takeoff at tick 2: drive upward off the floor, shoulders rise and both empty arms begin reaching above the head; one knee lifts while the other leg extends.
2. Airborne reach at tick 4: clearly airborne with a long upward reach, lead arm high and open, other arm raised for balance; both hands empty and separated from her hair.
3. REBOUND GRAB at simulation tick 5: highest two-hand rebound contact pose, both arms extended overhead and both open empty hands raised around the same unseen catch point with a clear transparent gap between palms and fingers; keep fingers above and away from the orange ponytail. This is the single grab frame.
4. LAND / SECURE at tick 7: descend into a balanced bent-knee landing and draw both empty hands together near the upper chest/sternum, visibly distinct from the overhead grab. Finish stable and in control.

The ball is a separate Piper-specific runtime object and must never be painted into the athlete art. Keep hands visibly empty in every pose. Do not draw any ball, sphere, seams, prop, hoop, rim, floor, court, ground shadow, glow, scenery, background color, checkerboard, grid, cell dividers, border, text, logo, label, UI, teammate, or extra person. Preserve genuine alpha-zero empty background, gutters and unused cell. Return only the transparent sheet.
provenance.cleanupNotes: Global alpha>=64 connected-component isolation retains five whole bodies including the original frame3 extension across the raw row boundary; removes all detached background glow/specks; drops alpha<12 outside one-pixel edge dilation; premultiplied-alpha Lanczos resizing uniformly fits each full silhouette within 380x380; centers in transparent 512px cells. No drawing, synthesis, duplication, or pose reordering.

review.sourceNotes: Five full ordered poses; 3x2 row-major, cell5 empty; Piper identity/anatomy preserved; no ball; clean alpha after glow removal; >=66 fully transparent px margins all four sides; frame3 source extension retained whole.
review.nativeTrackNotes: Production atlas selected for all five frames in both facings at 100% and 120%. The separate ball is carried at frame3/tick5 and aligns with the overhead two-hand catch; at frame4/tick7 it remains visible in Piper’s clasped upper-chest hands. No further adjustment recommended.
